precepts.text: Then Solomon began to build the house of the Lord at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where the Lord appeared unto David his father. Moriah: Moor right there, black again. The hill of the Moors was part of Jerusalem.
precepts.point: The word of the Lord that came to Micah the Morasthite: the word Moor, Morasthite, is in the Bible. Micah, teacher of the Moors.
precepts.why:
This shows that the hill of the Morasthites was part of Jerusalem: “Then Solomon began to build the house of the Lord at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where the Lord appeared unto David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.” Moriah: Moor right there, black again.

The reference work read in class says the same. Moriah was a hill adjacent to Jerusalem, on the northeast. There Abraham offered his son, in Genesis 22, and when Solomon built the temple on it, it became included in the city.

So the temple of the Lord stood on the hill of the Moors, and Micah the Morasthite, the teacher of the Moors, was a prophet of that same people. The Moors were Israelites; the names Moors and Africa came later, but the land and the house of the Lord tie them to Jerusalem.

precepts.text: The angel commanded David to set up an altar unto the Lord in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.
precepts.point: These are the things wherein Solomon was instructed for the building of the house of God: the length was threescore cubits, the breadth twenty cubits, and the porch in front was twenty cubits long according to the breadth of the house, and the height was a hundred and twenty. He overlaid it within with pure gold.
precepts.why:
“Then the angel of the Lord commanded Gad to say to David, that David should go up, and set up an altar unto the Lord in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.” This is the threshingfloor read of a few days ago in First Chronicles 21.

That same ground is where Solomon built. He “began to build the house of the Lord at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where the Lord appeared unto David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.” The altar David set up at the angel’s command marked the place of the house of God.

Solomon began “in the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign”, and these “are the things wherein Solomon was instructed for the building of the house of God”: threescore cubits long, twenty cubits broad, the porch twenty cubits by the breadth of the house, “and the height was an hundred and twenty: and he overlaid it within with pure gold.” Chronicles mixes here what is in First Kings 6 and 7, and Kings goes into much more detail on the building.

precepts.text: Solomon carved all the walls of the house round about with carved figures of cherubims, palm trees, and open flowers.
precepts.point: He made the most holy house twenty cubits long and twenty broad, overlaid with fine gold to the amount of six hundred talents, and the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers also with gold.
precepts.why:
Kings gives the fuller picture of the walls: “he carved all the walls of the house round about with carved figures of cherubims and palm trees and open flowers, within and without.” That is what Chronicles means when it says he “graved cherubims on the walls”.

Solomon cieled the greater house “with fir tree, which he overlaid with fine gold, and set thereon palm trees and chains.” He “garnished the house with precious stones for beauty: and the gold was gold of Parvaim.” He overlaid “the house, the beams, the posts, and the walls thereof, and the doors thereof, with gold”, real gold through and through, not the counterfeit metal of today.

So the house of the Lord itself was carved round about with figures, by the king who built it for the Most High. Solomon was not bowing down to the cherubims and images he made.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not make a graven image to bow down thyself to it nor serve it; the command forbids worship, not the carving.
precepts.point: He made the most holy house twenty cubits long and twenty broad, overlaid with fine gold to the amount of six hundred talents, and the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers also with gold.
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth”. Our unlearned Christian brothers and sisters, and some in other doctrines, say from this that a man cannot have images at all. But that is not what the Bible says.

The command forbids making a graven image to bow down thyself to it and serve it. It forbids the worship, not the mere carving of a figure. That is why Solomon could grave “cherubims on the walls” of the house of the Lord and not break the law: he was not bowing down to them.

precepts.text: Cursed is the man that maketh a graven or molten image and putteth it in a secret place, a hidden thing worshipped in secret.
precepts.point: He made the most holy house twenty cubits long and twenty broad, overlaid with fine gold to the amount of six hundred talents, and the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers also with gold.
precepts.why:
“Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Lord, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place.” The curse falls on the image made and put in a secret place, a hidden thing worshipped in secret.

A wall in a man’s house is not a secret place. It is seen plainly when a man enters the home; it is not hidden. Solomon’s cherubims were graved on the walls of the house of the Lord, open for all to see, not hidden away to be worshipped in the dark.

precepts.text: The prophet dug in the wall and found a hidden door leading to a chamber of secret idolatry.
precepts.point: He made the most holy house twenty cubits long and twenty broad, overlaid with fine gold to the amount of six hundred talents, and the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers also with gold.
precepts.why:
“Son of man, dig now in the wall: and when I had digged in the wall, behold a door.” The Lord had the prophet dig through a wall, and there was a hidden door leading to a chamber of secret idolatry.

That is what a secret place is: something hidden behind the wall, that has to be dug into to be found. It is the opposite of cherubims graved openly on the walls of the house of the Lord.

precepts.text: The ancients of Israel did their idolatry in the dark chambers of their imagery, saying the Lord seeth them not.
precepts.point: He made the most holy house twenty cubits long and twenty broad, overlaid with fine gold to the amount of six hundred talents, and the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers also with gold.
precepts.why:
Behind that hidden door the Lord showed the prophet “what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.”

That is the abomination: worshipping images in secret, in the dark, thinking the Lord does not see. It is not the goodly images made openly for the house of the Lord. The ancients of Israel hid their idols in chambers; Solomon graved his cherubims on the walls for everyone to see, and did not bow to them.

precepts.text: According to the goodness of the land Israel made goodly images; such were made openly for the house of the Lord.
precepts.point: He made the most holy house twenty cubits long and twenty broad, overlaid with fine gold to the amount of six hundred talents, and the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers also with gold.
precepts.why:
“Israel is an empty vine, he bringeth forth fruit unto himself: according to the multitude of his fruit he hath increased the altars; according to the goodness of his land they have made goodly images.”

According to the goodness of the land, Israel made goodly images, and these goodly images are the very ones read of here in the building of the house of the Lord: the cherubims graved on the walls, the palm trees and chains, the house garnished “with precious stones for beauty”. They were made openly for the house of the Lord, and Solomon was not bowing down to them.

And the house was rich with the goodness of the land: in the most holy house he “overlaid it with fine gold, amounting to six hundred talents. And the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. And he overlaid the upper chambers with gold.”

points: Solomon began to build the house of the Lord at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where the Lord appeared unto David his father, in the place David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite. This threshingfloor was read of a few days ago in First Chronicles 21.
He began to build in the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign. There is a mix here of First Kings 6 and 7, but Kings goes into much more detail on the building.

These are the things wherein Solomon was instructed for the building of the house of God: the length was threescore cubits, the breadth twenty cubits, and the porch in front was twenty cubits long according to the breadth of the house, and the height was a hundred and twenty. He overlaid it within with pure gold.

The greater house Solomon cieled with fir tree, overlaid with fine gold, and set thereon palm trees and chains. He garnished the house with precious stones for beauty, and the gold was gold of Parvaim. He overlaid the house, the beams, the posts, the walls, and the doors with gold, even real gold through and through, not the counterfeit metal of today.

He graved cherubims on the walls. Our unlearned Christian brothers and sisters, and some in other doctrines, say a man cannot have images at all, but that is not what the Bible says. The command in Exodus 20 forbids making a graven image to bow down to and serve, not the mere carving of a figure.
Solomon was not bowing down to the cherubims and images he made. Hosea 10 speaks of goodly images, and these goodly images are the very ones read of here in the building of the house of the Lord.

Ezekiel 8 shows what a secret place is: the Lord had the prophet dig through a wall into a hidden chamber where the ancients of Israel practiced idolatry in the dark, saying the Lord seeth us not. That is the abomination, worshipping images in secret, not the goodly images made openly for the house of the Lord.

He made the most holy house twenty cubits long and twenty broad, overlaid with fine gold to the amount of six hundred talents, and the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers also with gold.

In the most holy house Solomon made two cherubims of image work and overlaid them with gold. The wings of the cherubims were twenty cubits long altogether, each wing five cubits, one wing reaching to the wall and the other joining to the wing of the other cherub, and they stood on their feet with their faces inward.
He made the vail of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, and wrought cherubims thereon. Even the vail bore the figures of the cherubims, made openly for the service of the Most High.

He made before the house two pillars thirty and five cubits high, and the chapiter on the top of each was five cubits. He made chains as in the oracle and put them on the heads of the pillars, and made a hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.

He reared up the pillars before the temple, one on the right hand and the other on the left, and called the name of the one on the right Jachin and the name of the one on the left Boaz. This same detail is read in First Kings chapter 7.
